title: EON Office application manifest (v0 — UNSTABLE)
description: What an EON Office application tells the core, and the person installing it: who it is, which protocol versions it speaks, what it needs (capabilities), what it offers other applications (provides) and which events it emits (publishes). Installing grants nothing: every capability starts pending until the owner grants it, and a grant can only cover something listed here. Unknown fields are refused, so a typo is an error rather than a silently ignored line. eon-office-core's manifest reader enforces the same rules; the examples in this repository are run against both.

appId.description: Reverse-DNS, lowercase: at least two labels of a-z 0-9 and inner hyphens. Example: org.eon.office.notes.

name.description: Method and event names, collection names, ids, keys: 1-128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -. Narrow on purpose: these end up in logs and audit entries, and none of them is prose.

capability.description: See docs/capabilities.md. call:<app-id> allows calling the methods that application provides.

name.description: What the person sees, e.g. "EON Notes".

version.description: Semantic version (semver.org 2.0.0). Upgrades never go backwards (madde 39).

api.description: The protocol versions this application speaks, inclusive. The core refuses an application whose range does not contain its own version.

entry.description: How the core starts the application. A relative command is resolved against the application's install path. Absent: the application starts on its own and connects; the core cannot launch it.

provides.description: Methods other applications may call through the core with call:<this id>. Calling anything not listed is refused by the core before it reaches the application.

publishes.description: Event names this application emits, under <id>/. Publishing anything else is refused, so every event is documented here.

restart.description: What the core's supervisor does when the application exits with a failure. on-failure: restart, at most three times a minute, with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s back-off.
